sentences.text: Machairoceratops cronusi is the only known species in its genus, a four-legged herbivore that possessed a frill to protect its neck.

Its genus name means "bent sword" because of the two forward-curving horns located at the top of its frill, while the species name cronusi honors the Greek god Cronus, who is depicted in mythology carrying a curved sickle.

The top of its skull featured a single pair of long, curved spikes that were 44 centimeters long, and its postorbital horns measured 27 centimeters in length, though their exact orientation on the skull is unknown.
Unlike other centrosaurines, the sides of its frill lacked smaller epiparietal bones.
The holotype specimen is approximately the same size as the dinosaur Diabloceratops.
The animal is known only from the holotype specimen UMNH VP 20550, discovered in 2006 and now held at the Natural History Museum of Utah.

Researchers tested its position within the subfamily Centrosaurinae using maximum parsimony and Bayesian phylogenetic analyses, where the maximum parsimony analysis resulted in a large polytomy at the base of Centrosaurinae, resolving only specific subgroups like Centrosaurini and a clade of Avaceratops and Nasutoceratops, while the Bayesian analysis produced a fully resolved evolutionary tree.

This extinct centrosaurine dinosaur lived during the Late Cretaceous in the Wahweap Formation of southern Utah, United States, with the precise age of the animal estimated to be 80.06 million years ago, with an uncertainty range between 80.68 and 79.26 million years ago.

When it lived, the Western Interior Seaway was at its widest, nearly isolating southern Laramidia from the rest of North America, and its habitat included lakes, floodplains, and rivers flowing to the east where the climate was wet and seasonal.
